references.text: The peace offering (שְׁלָמִים) is described in detail in Leviticus, where the laws for this offering are given.
Detailed instructions on the peace offering and how it was to be brought before the Lord.
The first time the peace offering with the same number of animals is mentioned is in connection with the gifts of the tribal leaders.
Nethanel's peace offering follows the same pattern with two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old lambs.
Eliab's peace offering follows an identical pattern, showing unity among the tribes in their gifts.
Elisur, son of Shedeur, is mentioned as the leader of the tribe of Reuben at the census.
Elisur, son of Shedeur, was the leader of Reuben's camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
Elisur led the tribe of Reuben when they broke camp from the encampment.
Peace offerings were also brought at the covenant ceremony at Sinai.
The peace offering was part of the priestly consecration and the service of the tabernacle.
